title: Oh, well! #broadway #ohmary #mayarudolph #coleescola
transcript: I couldn't resist Maya Rudolph, so I saw Oh Mary for the second time over two years after seeing it off Broadway. And seeing it again with someone besides Cole Escola in the role kind of reaffirmed some of the reservations I had about it from the beginning. To be clear, though, that's not a knock against Maya Rudolph. She's pretty much everything I hope she'd be. The character is obviously written to be very petulant, but where Cole Escola played it more like a melodramatic airhead, Maya Rudolph's take on it was like a whiny, sarcastic teenage girl that never grew up. And obviously she's able to incorporate some of her own sense of humor and just her natural skill with comedy overall. And yet, no matter how hard I tried, I couldn't might get Cole Escola's voice, their delivery, their comedic choices out of my head throughout the show. Which kind of confirmed the suspicion that I had from the moment I walked out of the Lucille Lortel two years and three months ago that Escola’s performance was kind of the glue holding this whole production together, at least for me and my enjoyment of it. Obviously, that's not the case with audiences at large. I mean, the proof is in the pudding. It's been massive hit with lots of people in the role. It secured a London transfer, a tour. It was a Pulitzer finalist, for God's sake. And I'm happy for them, I really am. I Wish I liked this play more than I do, which isn't to say that I dislike it. I like the overall subversive concept, and even without Escola in the role, I do think the character of Mary is exceptionally well written. Every time she opens her mouth, it's hysterically funny. But every time she closes her mouth or is off stage, I just kind of detach from the play a little. In particular, I feel like this running joke of, like, “what if Lincoln were gay?” Is just not that funny to me. And it's kind of a one joke subplot that takes up a lot more airtime than I think it warrants. And I felt that the first time I saw it a little bit, but even more so the second time, when some of the novelty had worn off. That said, I definitely don't regret seeing it again. And if it had to be anybody, I'm so happy it was Maya Rudolph. But I do think two times is enough for me, which I'm sure no one is crying about. I mean, more tickets for everyone else.
classificationReason: Creator saw Oh, Mary! on Broadway a second time (first was off-Broadway), now with Maya Rudolph in the lead role, and shares detailed first-hand opinions comparing performances and reservations about the production.
